# `silk/system/subprocess`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start a child process whose standard streams stay open while it runs, send it signals, and learn
when it ends through a descriptor that an event loop can watch.

## When to use
Use [`Subprocess.spawn`](#Subprocess.impl.spawn) when your program talks to the child while it runs, as a JavaScript
runtime or a shell does: you get the process ID and the parent end of each pipe as raw
descriptors, and you read and write them in your own loop. To run a program to the end and get
all of its output, use the `ChildProcess` effect from `silk.system.child_process` instead.

## Details
A [`ProcessRequest`](./system-child-process.md#ProcessRequest) from `silk.system.child_process` gives the program, the arguments, the
environment, and the working directory. [`SpawnOptions`](#SpawnOptions) gives the rest: what the child gets in
each descriptor slot ([`Stdio`](#Stdio)), the first argument, a new session, and the user and group.

Every call returns at once. Nothing in this module waits for the child:
- The parent end of each [`Stdio.pipe`](#Stdio.impl.pipe) slot is a nonblocking, close-on-exec UNIX stream socket.
- [`ExitWatch.open`](#ExitWatch.impl.open) gives a descriptor that becomes readable when the child ends: a pidfd on
  Linux, and a kqueue with an `EVFILT_PROC` filter on Darwin. Register it with a reactor, such
  as `silk.io.reactor`, next to the pipes.
- [`ExitWatch.collect`](#ExitWatch.impl.collect) collects the exit status once the exit descriptor is readable.
  [`Subprocess.tryWait`](#Subprocess.impl.tryWait) collects it if the child has ended, or returns `none` if it still runs.

The child starts with every signal unblocked, and with the default action for every signal that
can be caught, so a signal that the parent blocks or ignores reaches the child normally.

## Errors
Each operation fails with [`SubprocessError`](#SubprocessError): the [`SubprocessOperation`](#SubprocessOperation) and the native error
code, such as 2 (`ENOENT`) when the program does not exist.

## Gotchas
- Collect the status after the child ends, or the child stays a zombie process.
- Collect the status of a child in one place only. A second `waitpid` for the same child, from
  other code, takes the status away.
- A program is a path. This module does not search `PATH`.
- On GNU/Linux, a child with a working directory, a user, or a group starts with `fork`, which
  is slower for a large parent. Darwin uses `fork` only for a user or a group.
- On GNU/Linux, a child started without `fork` also gets each descriptor that the parent itself
  inherited without close-on-exec.
- The module is empty on targets other than Darwin on x86_64 or aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc
  on x86_64 or aarch64.

## Examples
### Read the output of a child and wait for its exit
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.mem.pointer { Pointer }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.system.child_process { ChildProcess }
import silk.system.filesystem { FileError, Path }
import silk.system.subprocess { ExitStatus, ExitWatch, SpawnOptions, Stdio, Subprocess, SubprocessError }

extern "C" struct PollFd { fd: i32, events: i16, revents: i16 }
static if Intrinsic.targetOperatingSystem() == "darwin" {
  @foreign(noCapture: .("fds"))
  unsafe extern "C" fn poll(fds: ?[*]mut PollFd, count: u32, timeout: i32) -> i32
} else {
  @foreign(noCapture: .("fds"))
  unsafe extern "C" fn poll(fds: ?[*]mut PollFd, count: usize, timeout: i32) -> i32
}
@foreign(noCapture: .("buffer"))
unsafe extern "C" fn read(fd: i32, buffer: ?[*]mut u8, count: usize) -> isize

effect fn program() -> i32 ! FileError | SubprocessError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let path = run Path.make("/bin/echo")
  let mut request = run ChildProcess.request(&path)
  run ChildProcess.addArgument(&mut request, "hi")
  let mut options = SpawnOptions.make()
  run options.setStdio(1, Stdio.pipe())
  let mut child = run Subprocess.spawn(&request, &options)
  let output = match child.takePipe(1) {
    Option<i32>.Some { value } => value
    Option<i32>.None => { return 1 }
  }
  let watch = run ExitWatch.open(child.pid())

  // Wait for the exit descriptor; a real program registers it with a reactor instead.
  let mut watched = [PollFd { fd: watch.descriptor(), events: 1, revents: 0 }]
  let _ready = unsafe poll(Pointer.fromMutSlice<PollFd>(&mut watched), 1, -1)
  let status = run watch.collect()

  // echo has ended, so its output is in the socket.
  let mut bytes: [u8; 8] = [0; 8]
  let count = unsafe read(output, Pointer.fromMutSlice<u8>(&mut bytes), 8)
  Subprocess.closeDescriptor(output)
  if status.signaled || status.code != 0 || count != 3 || bytes[0] != 104 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let result = run Effect.result(program()) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return match move result {
    Result<i32, FileError | SubprocessError | OutOfMemoryError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<i32, FileError | SubprocessError | OutOfMemoryError>.Failure { .. } => 1
  }
}
```

A failed operation of this module: which one, and the native error code.

### Details
`code` is the `errno` value of the failed system call, such as 2 (`ENOENT`) when the program
does not exist, 13 (`EACCES`) when it cannot be run, 3 (`ESRCH`) when no process has the ID, or
22 (`EINVAL`) for a request with a NUL byte or an empty program.

<a id="Stdio.impl.ignore"></a>

### Associated function `ignore`

```silk
pub fn ignore() -> Stdio
```

Returns a slot that the child does not get from the parent.

#### Details
Slots 0, 1, and 2 are opened on `/dev/null` in the child, so a read sees the end at once and a
write is discarded. A higher slot is not opened by this module.

<a id="Stdio.impl.inherit"></a>

### Associated function `inherit`

```silk
pub fn inherit(fd: i32) -> Stdio
```

Returns a slot that the child gets as a copy of the parent's descriptor `fd`.

#### Details
The parent keeps `fd` open and owns it. `fd` can be any open descriptor, such as the
parent's own standard output, a file, or a socket. [`Subprocess.spawn`](#Subprocess.impl.spawn) fails with code 9
(`EBADF`) if `fd` is not open.

<a id="Stdio.impl.pipe"></a>

### Associated function `pipe`

```silk
pub fn pipe() -> Stdio
```

Returns a slot connected to a new pipe between the parent and the child.

#### Details
The pipe is a UNIX stream socket pair, so both sides can read and write, and it can carry
descriptors with `SCM_RIGHTS`. The parent end is nonblocking and close-on-exec. Take it with
[`Subprocess.takePipe`](#Subprocess.impl.takePipe). The child end is blocking, as programs expect.

## `SpawnOptions`

```silk
pub struct SpawnOptions
```

How [`Subprocess.spawn`](#Subprocess.impl.spawn) starts a child, apart from the [`ProcessRequest`](./system-child-process.md#ProcessRequest).

### Details
[`SpawnOptions.make`](#SpawnOptions.impl.make) gives slots 0, 1, and 2 as [`Stdio.ignore`](#Stdio.impl.ignore), the program path as the
first argument, the session, user, and group of the parent.

<a id="SpawnOptions.impl.setStdio"></a>

### Method `setStdio`

```silk
pub effect fn setStdio(self: &mut Self, slot: usize, stdio: Stdio) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Sets what the child gets in descriptor `slot`, such as 0 for standard input.

#### Details
Each slot below `slot` that is not set is [`Stdio.ignore`](#Stdio.impl.ignore). The child gets slots 0, 1, and 2,
and each higher slot that you set. Each other descriptor of the parent is closed in the child,
except as the module gotchas say for GNU/Linux.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the slot list.

<a id="ExitStatus"></a>

## `ExitStatus`

```silk
pub struct ExitStatus
```

How an ended child ended, from [`Subprocess.tryWait`](#Subprocess.impl.tryWait).

### Details
When `signaled` is false, the child exited and `code` is its exit code from 0 to 255, and
`signal` is 0. When `signaled` is true, a signal ended the child: `signal` is its number, such
as 9 for `SIGKILL`, and `code` is 0.

<a id="Subprocess"></a>

## `Subprocess`

```silk
pub struct Subprocess
```

A started child: its process ID and the parent ends of its pipes.

### Details
The value owns each pipe end until you take it with [`Subprocess.takePipe`](#Subprocess.impl.takePipe); dropping the value
closes the pipe ends that were not taken. Dropping it does not stop the child and does not
collect its status.

### Gotchas
Call [`Subprocess.tryWait`](#Subprocess.impl.tryWait) after the child ends, or the child stays a zombie process.

<a id="Subprocess.impl.spawn"></a>

### Associated function `spawn`

```silk
pub effect fn spawn(request: &ProcessRequest, options: &SpawnOptions) -> Subprocess ! SubprocessError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Starts the program of `request` with `options`, and returns at once.

#### Details
The child gets the arguments and the environment of `request`, and its working directory, or
the parent's when it has none. Each descriptor slot gets what [`SpawnOptions.setStdio`](#SpawnOptions.impl.setStdio) set.
The child starts with every signal unblocked and with the default action for each signal
that can be caught.

A failure to start, such as a program that does not exist, is an error of this call; no
child is left.

#### Errors
- [`SubprocessError`](#SubprocessError) with operation `Spawn` and the native code, such as 2 (`ENOENT`) for a
  missing program or working directory, 13 (`EACCES`), 1 (`EPERM`) for a user or group change
  that is not allowed, 9 (`EBADF`) for a [`Stdio.inherit`](#Stdio.impl.inherit) descriptor that is not open, or 22
  (`EINVAL`) for an empty program or a NUL byte in the request.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies of the request.

#### Gotchas
This function does not search `PATH`. Give the full path of the program.

### Method `takePipe`

```silk
pub fn takePipe(self: &mut Self, slot: usize) -> Option<i32>
```

Takes the parent end of the pipe in `slot`, or returns `none` if `slot` is not a
[`Stdio.pipe`](#Stdio.impl.pipe) slot or its end was taken before.

#### Details
The end is a nonblocking, close-on-exec UNIX stream socket. You own it: close it with
[`Subprocess.closeDescriptor`](#Subprocess.impl.closeDescriptor) or other code.

<a id="Subprocess.impl.closeDescriptor"></a>

### Associated function `closeDescriptor`

```silk
pub fn closeDescriptor(fd: i32) -> ()
```

Closes the descriptor `fd` that you took with [`Subprocess.takePipe`](#Subprocess.impl.takePipe). A descriptor that is
not open is ignored.

<a id="Subprocess.impl.kill"></a>

### Associated function `kill`

```silk
pub effect fn kill(pid: i32, signal: i32) -> () ! SubprocessError
```

Sends `signal` to the process `pid`, such as 15 for `SIGTERM`.

#### Details
A negative `pid` sends the signal to each process of the process group `-pid`, such as a
group that a [`SpawnOptions.setDetached`](#SpawnOptions.impl.setDetached) child leads. Signal 0 sends nothing and checks
that the process exists.

#### Errors
[`SubprocessError`](#SubprocessError) with operation `Kill`, for example with code 3 (`ESRCH`) if no process has
the ID, 1 (`EPERM`) if the caller may not signal it, or 22 (`EINVAL`) for a signal that does
not exist.

<a id="Subprocess.impl.tryWait"></a>

### Associated function `tryWait`

```silk
pub effect fn tryWait(pid: i32) -> Option<ExitStatus> ! SubprocessError
```

Collects the exit status of the child `pid` if it has ended, and returns `none` if it still
runs. It never blocks.

#### Details
After a status is returned, the process ID is free and can belong to a new process, so do not
signal or wait for `pid` again. A stopped child counts as running.

#### Errors
[`SubprocessError`](#SubprocessError) with operation `Wait`, for example with code 10 (`ECHILD`) if `pid` is not
a child of this process or its status was collected before.

<a id="ExitWatch"></a>

## `ExitWatch`

```silk
pub struct ExitWatch
```

A descriptor that becomes readable when a child process ends.

### When to use
Open one for each child that you start with [`Subprocess.spawn`](#Subprocess.impl.spawn), and register
[`ExitWatch.descriptor`](#ExitWatch.impl.descriptor) with a reactor for reads. When it is readable, call
[`ExitWatch.collect`](#ExitWatch.impl.collect) and drop the watch.

### Details
The descriptor is a pidfd on Linux and a kqueue with an `EVFILT_PROC` exit filter on Darwin. It
is close-on-exec. It stays readable after the child ends; do not read from it. Dropping the
watch closes it.

### Gotchas
- Open the watch before you collect the status of the child. After that, the process ID can
  belong to another process.
- On Darwin the descriptor can become readable while the kernel still finishes the exit, so
  [`Subprocess.tryWait`](#Subprocess.impl.tryWait) can still return `none` then. [`ExitWatch.collect`](#ExitWatch.impl.collect) waits for that
  short step.
- On Linux, pidfds need kernel 5.3 or later.

<a id="ExitWatch.impl.collect"></a>

### Method `collect`

```silk
pub effect fn collect(self: &Self) -> ExitStatus ! SubprocessError
```

Collects the exit status of the watched child after [`ExitWatch.descriptor`](#ExitWatch.impl.descriptor) is readable.

#### Details
The child has ended when the descriptor is readable. On Linux the status is ready then, and
the call returns at once. On Darwin the kernel reports the exit a moment before the status is
ready, and the call waits for the kernel to finish the exit. After it returns, the process ID
is free, as after [`Subprocess.tryWait`](#Subprocess.impl.tryWait).

#### Errors
[`SubprocessError`](#SubprocessError) with operation `Wait`, for example with code 10 (`ECHILD`) if the status
was collected before.

#### Gotchas
- Before the descriptor is readable, the call blocks until the child ends.
